title: Numbers Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Numbers chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Numbers Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Numbers Chapter 21.

questions.question: Who was the king that fought against Israel and took some prisoners?
questions.correctAnswer: King Arad
questions.explanation: King Arad the Canaanite fought against Israel and took some prisoners as stated in Numbers 21:1.

questions.question: What vow did Israel make to the LORD after being attacked?
questions.correctAnswer: To utterly destroy their cities
questions.explanation: Israel vowed to utterly destroy the cities of their enemies if the LORD delivered them, as recorded in Numbers 21:2.

questions.question: What name was given to the place where Israel destroyed the Canaanites and their cities?
questions.correctAnswer: Hormah
questions.explanation: The place was named Hormah after the LORD delivered the Canaanites into Israel's hand and they destroyed them, as per Numbers 21:3.

questions.question: From which location did Israel journey by the way of the Red Sea to compass Edom?
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Hor
questions.explanation: Israel journeyed from Mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea to compass Edom according to Numbers 21:4.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Israel were encouraged and joyful because of the way during their journey from Mount Hor.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way as stated in Numbers 21:4.

questions.question: What complaint did the people of Israel make against God and Moses?
options: Why bring us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness?
Why have you made us slaves again?
Why do we have no kings?
Why do we have to fight our enemies?
questions.correctAnswer: Why bring us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: The people asked why they were brought up out of Egypt only to die in the wilderness due to lack of bread and water as in Numbers 21:5.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and many died.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and many of Israel died as recorded in Numbers 21:6.

questions.question: What did the people ask Moses to do after the serpents bit them?
options: Pray to the LORD to take away the serpents
questions.correctAnswer: Pray to the LORD to take away the serpents
questions.explanation: The people asked Moses to pray to the LORD to remove the serpents, as stated in Numbers 21:7.

questions.question: What did the LORD instruct Moses to make to heal those bitten by serpents?
options: A fiery serpent and set it on a pole
questions.correctAnswer: A fiery serpent and set it on a pole
questions.explanation: The LORD told Moses to make a fiery serpent and set it upon a pole so that those bitten who looked at it would live, as in Numbers 21:8.

questions.question: True or False: Moses made a serpent of brass and put it on a pole, and those who looked at it after being bitten lived.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Moses made a serpent of brass and set it on a pole; those who looked at it lived after being bitten, according to Numbers 21:9.

questions.question: Where did the children of Israel pitch their tents after setting forward from the place of the brass serpent?
questions.correctAnswer: Oboth
questions.explanation: The children of Israel pitched in Oboth after setting forward as noted in Numbers 21:10.

questions.question: What is the correct order of Israel's encampments after leaving Oboth?
questions.correctAnswer: Ijeabarim, Valley of Zared
questions.explanation: Israel journeyed from Oboth to pitch at Ijeabarim, then removed to pitch in the valley of Zared, as per Numbers 21:11-12.

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites journeyed toward the sunrising when they pitched at Ijeabarim.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The Israelites pitched at Ijeabarim in the wilderness before Moab, toward the sunrising as stated in Numbers 21:11.

questions.question: What did the people of Israel say about the bread they received in the wilderness?
options: Our soul loatheth this light bread
This bread is delicious and sustaining
We want to return to Egypt for bread
questions.correctAnswer: Our soul loatheth this light bread
questions.explanation: The people said their soul loathed the light bread, referring to manna, as in Numbers 21:5.

questions.question: What was the people's reaction after the LORD sent fiery serpents among them?
options: They confessed their sin and asked Moses to pray for them
questions.correctAnswer: They confessed their sin and asked Moses to pray for them
questions.explanation: The people recognized their sin and asked Moses to pray for the removal of the serpents as seen in Numbers 21:7.

medium.title: Numbers Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Numbers Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What geographic feature marked the border between Moab and the Amorites according to Numbers 21?
questions.correctAnswer: Arnon
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:13 states that Arnon is the border between Moab and the Amorites, marking a significant geographical boundary.

questions.question: In Numbers 21, what is the significance of the 'book of the wars of the LORD' as mentioned in verse 14?
options: It records Israel’s victories in battles including Red Sea and Arnon
It contains laws given to Moses
It is a book of songs and praises
questions.correctAnswer: It records Israel’s victories in battles including Red Sea and Arnon
questions.explanation: Verse 14 refers to the 'book of the wars of the LORD' which recounts what God did in the Red Sea and the brooks of Arnon, highlighting divine intervention in battles.

questions.question: What did the Israelites do at Beer, and how does this demonstrate their trust in God's provision?
options: They gathered around the well as God had promised water
They built an altar to celebrate victory
They prepared for battle against Sihon
questions.correctAnswer: They gathered around the well as God had promised water
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:16 shows that at Beer, the Israelites gathered as God had instructed Moses, demonstrating faith and obedience to God's promise of water provision.

questions.question: How does the song sung by Israel at Beer reflect a biblical virtue?
options: It expresses gratitude and praise to God for provision
It calls for judgment against enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It expresses gratitude and praise to God for provision
questions.explanation: In Numbers 21:17, Israel sings to the well, symbolizing thankfulness and worship, highlighting the virtue of gratitude towards God’s faithfulness.

questions.question: Who directed the digging of the well at Beer, and what does this teach about leadership?
options: The princes and nobles under the lawgiver's direction
questions.correctAnswer: The princes and nobles under the lawgiver's direction
questions.explanation: Verse 18 shows that leadership involved cooperation between leaders and the lawgiver (Moses), teaching the importance of organized and obedient leadership in God's work.

questions.question: What was Israel’s request to Sihon king of the Amorites, and what does this reveal about their attitude?
options: To pass through without harming land or water, showing respect and peace
To join them in battle against Moab
questions.correctAnswer: To pass through without harming land or water, showing respect and peace
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:22 reveals Israel's respectful request to Sihon, illustrating integrity and peaceful intentions even when traveling through foreign land.

questions.question: What was Sihon’s response to Israel’s request, and what does this teach about obedience to God’s guidance?
options: He refused and attacked Israel, leading to battle
He allowed Israel to pass peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: He refused and attacked Israel, leading to battle
questions.explanation: According to Numbers 21:23, Sihon’s refusal and aggression contrasts with Israel’s obedience and trust in God's guidance to take the land by force when necessary.

questions.question: What was the outcome of Israel’s battle with Sihon, and how does it demonstrate God’s faithfulness?
options: Israel defeated Sihon and possessed his land
questions.correctAnswer: Israel defeated Sihon and possessed his land
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:24 shows Israel’s victory and possession of Sihon’s land, demonstrating God's faithfulness to His promises when His people act in obedience and faith.

questions.question: How does the possession of land from Arnon to Jabbok illustrate God’s provision for His people?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:24 explains that Israel possessed the land from Arnon unto Jabbok, illustrating God's provision and fulfillment of His promise to give the Israelites a place to dwell.

questions.question: According to Numbers 21, did Israel take possession of all the cities of the Amorites?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 25 confirms that Israel took all the cities of the Amorites and dwelt in them, showing complete victory and fulfillment of God’s promise.

questions.question: Was Heshbon originally the city of Moab before being taken by Sihon king of the Amorites?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:26 states that Heshbon was the city of Sihon, who had taken it from the former king of Moab, indicating it was originally Moabite land but owned by the Amorites at the time.

questions.question: What does the proverb mentioned in Numbers 21:27 encourage people to do regarding Heshbon?
options: Come into Heshbon and prepare the city
Avoid Heshbon because it is cursed
questions.correctAnswer: Come into Heshbon and prepare the city
questions.explanation: Verse 27 cites a proverb urging people to come into and prepare the city of Sihon, showing the importance of establishing and fortifying the conquered city.

questions.question: How does the description of fire and flame in Heshbon (verse 28) symbolize God’s judgment?
options: It represents destruction of Moab by Sihon's power
It signifies a festival of lights
It shows the city was warm and hospitable
questions.correctAnswer: It represents destruction of Moab by Sihon's power
questions.explanation: Verse 28’s metaphor of fire going out of Heshbon symbolizes the consuming judgment and defeat of Moab’s strongholds by Sihon and Israel, revealing God's justice.

questions.question: Based on Numbers 21:13-24, how does this passage teach about the virtue of faith during adversity?
options: By showing Israel’s trust in God to conquer strong enemies
By advising to avoid all conflicts
questions.correctAnswer: By showing Israel’s trust in God to conquer strong enemies
questions.explanation: The passage from verses 13 to 24 shows Israel facing strong enemies yet trusting God to deliver them and possess the land, illustrating faith and obedience amidst challenges.

questions.question: What does Numbers 21:22-24 promise will happen if Israel seeks peaceful passage through Sihon’s land but he refuses?
options: Israel will fight and possess Sihon’s land
Israel will build a wall around their camp
Israel will pay tribute to Sihon
questions.correctAnswer: Israel will fight and possess Sihon’s land
questions.explanation: Verses 22-24 explain that although Israel requested peaceful passage, Sihon’s refusal led to battle, where Israel defeated him and took possession of his territory, showing God’s provision when peace is denied.

hard.title: Numbers Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Numbers Chapter 21.

questions.question: Which city did Israel take and dwell in that was formerly the city of Sihon king of the Amorites?
questions.correctAnswer: Heshbon
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:25-26 states that Israel took all these cities and dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, specifically mentioning Heshbon as the city of Sihon king of the Amorites.

questions.question: What does the proverb say about the city of Sihon in Heshbon?
options: Come into Heshbon, let the city of Sihon be built and prepared
The walls of Heshbon are unbreakable
Heshbon is a city of refuge
questions.correctAnswer: Come into Heshbon, let the city of Sihon be built and prepared
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:27 quotes a proverb about the city of Sihon in Heshbon, inviting people to come into it and prepare it.

questions.question: What calamity is described as having gone out from Heshbon, consuming Ar of Moab and the lords of the high places of Arnon?
questions.correctAnswer: Fire
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:28 describes a fire gone out of Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon, which consumed Ar of Moab and the lords of the high places of Arnon.

questions.question: Who is the deity mentioned as the patron god of Moab, whose people were given into captivity by Sihon king of the Amorites?
questions.correctAnswer: Chemosh
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:29 refers to the people of Chemosh, the god of Moab, lamenting that their sons and daughters were given into captivity by Sihon king of the Amorites.

questions.question: Which king of Bashan opposed Israel in battle at Edrei?
questions.correctAnswer: Og
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:33 states that Og king of Bashan went out against Israel to battle at Edrei.

questions.question: What instruction did the LORD give Moses regarding Og king of Bashan?
options: Fear him not, for I have delivered him into thy hand
questions.correctAnswer: Fear him not, for I have delivered him into thy hand
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:34 records the LORD telling Moses not to fear Og because God had delivered him into Moses' hand, similar to what was done with Sihon.

questions.question: What was the outcome of Israel's battle with Og king of Bashan?
options: They smote him and all his people until none was left alive
questions.correctAnswer: They smote him and all his people until none was left alive
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:35 states that Israel smote Og, his sons, and all his people until none was left alive and they possessed his land.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Hormah' mean, the name given to the place where Israel utterly destroyed the Canaanites and their cities?
questions.correctAnswer: Destruction
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:3 shows that the place was called Hormah, which in Hebrew means 'destruction' or 'devoted to destruction,' referring to the utter destruction of the Canaanites there.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the narrative of the brass serpent Moses made, as described in Numbers 21:8-9?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: The brass serpent is a typology foreshadowing Christ being lifted up for salvation, as explained in John 3:14, showing a deeper theological meaning beyond the literal event in Numbers 21:8-9.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage explicitly connects and fulfills the theme of the brass serpent lifted up for healing, as introduced in Numbers 21?
questions.correctAnswer: John 3:14
questions.explanation: John 3:14 references the lifting up of the serpent in the wilderness as a foreshadowing of Jesus being lifted up on the cross for salvation, directly connecting to Numbers 21:8-9.

questions.question: How did Israel request to pass through the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, according to Numbers 21:22?
options: By not turning into fields or vineyards, not drinking water from wells, and traveling by the king's highway
questions.correctAnswer: By not turning into fields or vineyards, not drinking water from wells, and traveling by the king's highway
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:22 records Israel’s message to Sihon requesting passage without disturbing the land or water sources and traveling only by the king’s highway.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 21:23, Sihon king of the Amorites allowed Israel to pass peacefully through his lands.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:23 states that Sihon did not allow Israel to pass; instead, he gathered his people to fight against Israel.

questions.question: Who dug the well at Beer, according to Numbers 21:18, and under whose direction?
options: Princes and nobles of the people, by the direction of the lawgiver
The Levites, by God's direct command
The elders of Israel, by popular vote
questions.correctAnswer: Princes and nobles of the people, by the direction of the lawgiver
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:18 says the princes and nobles dug the well at Beer under the direction of the lawgiver (Moses).

questions.question: What geographical border is described as separating Moab and the Amorites in Numbers 21:13?
questions.correctAnswer: The river Arnon
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:13 indicates the Arnon river as the border between Moab and the Amorites.

questions.question: True or False: The narrative of Israel's battles with Sihon and Og in Numbers 21 demonstrates God's faithful provision of victory to His people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:34 and 35 show God assuring Moses that He has delivered Og into Israel’s hand and that they defeated him completely, illustrating God's faithfulness in granting victory.

theological.title: Numbers Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Numbers Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice is illustrated by God sending fiery serpents among the Israelites as described in Numbers 21:6?
options: God punishes sin but also provides a way for deliverance
God ignores the sins of His people
God rewards immediate obedience with blessings
God's punishment is always physical only
questions.correctAnswer: God punishes sin but also provides a way for deliverance
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:6 shows God sending fiery serpents as punishment for Israel's sin, while verses 7-9 reveal God provides a means of salvation through the brass serpent, illustrating both divine justice and mercy.

questions.question: According to Numbers 21:3, what was the significance of the place named Hormah?
options: It was where Israel defeated the Canaanites after God delivered them
It was the location of the fiery serpents
It was the well where God provided water
It was the city of King Sihon
questions.correctAnswer: It was where Israel defeated the Canaanites after God delivered them
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:3 states that after God delivered the Canaanites into Israel's hand, they utterly destroyed them and called the place Hormah, marking a significant divine victory.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by His response to Israel's complaint about bread and water in Numbers 21:5-7?
options: God's holiness and justice in punishing rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and justice in punishing rebellion
questions.explanation: In Numbers 21:5-7, Israel's complaint against God and Moses leads to God's just punishment by sending serpents, underscoring His holiness and intolerance of sin.

questions.question: How does the brass serpent Moses made (Numbers 21:8-9) serve as a Christological type in biblical theology?
options: It prefigures Christ being lifted up to bring salvation to sinners
It symbolizes the law that condemns sin
It represents Israel's idolatry in the wilderness
It foreshadows the destruction of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Christ being lifted up to bring salvation to sinners
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:8-9 describes the brass serpent lifted on a pole, healing those who look upon it, typologically pointing to Christ being lifted on the cross for humanity’s salvation (cf. John 3:14-15).

questions.question: What theological insight about God’s providence is conveyed by the journeying and encamping pattern of Israel in Numbers 21:10-20?
options: God guides His people step-by-step through wilderness challenges
Israel journeyed by their own wisdom and strength
The journey was aimless and without divine purpose
God abandoned Israel during their travels
questions.correctAnswer: God guides His people step-by-step through wilderness challenges
questions.explanation: The detailed encampments in Numbers 21:10-20 illustrate God’s providential leading of Israel through difficult terrain, highlighting His sustaining guidance in sanctification.

questions.question: What does Israel's request and Sihon's refusal in Numbers 21:21-23 reveal about human free will and divine sovereignty?
options: Human refusal to yield to God's people does not thwart divine plans
God forces all kings to submit without resistance
Israel always conquers by their own power
Divine sovereignty is limited by human decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Human refusal to yield to God's people does not thwart divine plans
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:21-23 shows Israel’s peaceful request denied by Sihon, yet God’s sovereignty ensures Israel’s victory despite human opposition, illustrating divine control over history.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification and possession of the promised land is taught by Israel taking Sihon's cities as in Numbers 21:24-26?
options: God grants His people victory as part of their sanctification and inheritance
Possession of land is by human conquest alone
Sanctification is unrelated to obedience and victory
God’s promises are conditional on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God grants His people victory as part of their sanctification and inheritance
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:24-26 shows God giving Israel victory over Sihon’s cities, demonstrating sanctification through obedience and God’s faithfulness in granting the promised inheritance.

questions.question: How does the lament over Moab in Numbers 21:28-29 reflect God's justice and covenant faithfulness?
options: God judges nations opposing His covenant people
God is indifferent to the fate of nations
God punishes Israel for their sins here
questions.correctAnswer: God judges nations opposing His covenant people
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:28-29 pronounces woe on Moab for their defeat, demonstrating God's justice in punishing those who oppose His covenant people, highlighting His faithfulness to Israel.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching do Numbers 21:6 and Numbers 21:8 convey regarding sin, judgment, and salvation?
options: Sin brings judgment, but God provides a means of salvation through faith
Judgment is final with no hope of salvation
Salvation is achieved by human effort alone
God ignores sin and does not judge
questions.correctAnswer: Sin brings judgment, but God provides a means of salvation through faith
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:6 shows God’s judgment by serpents for sin; 21:8 shows God commanding a brass serpent for healing, teaching that while sin incurs judgment, God graciously provides salvation for those who believe.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God’s sovereignty in battle is emphasized by God’s promise to Moses concerning Og king of Bashan in Numbers 21:34?
options: God sovereignly delivers enemies into His people's hands
Victory depends solely on Israel’s military strength
God is uncertain about outcomes of battles
God abandons His people in warfare
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly delivers enemies into His people's hands
questions.explanation: In Numbers 21:34, God assures Moses not to fear Og, promising delivery into Israel’s hands, affirming divine sovereignty over battles to fulfill His promises.

questions.question: How does the song sung by Israel at the well in Numbers 21:17-18 reflect their recognition of God's providential provision and leadership?
options: Israel praises God for providing water miraculously in the wilderness
Israel boasts of their own digging skills
Israel complains about the wilderness journey
questions.correctAnswer: Israel praises God for providing water miraculously in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:17-18 depicts Israel singing and praising the well God instructed them to dig, acknowledging His provision and guidance amid hardship.

questions.question: What does the record of Israel’s military conquests in Numbers 21:31-35 teach about God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises?
options: God fulfills His promises by granting victory and land to His people
God’s promises are often delayed and unfulfilled
Israel conquers by their own power without God’s help
God abandons Israel after initial victories
questions.correctAnswer: God fulfills His promises by granting victory and land to His people
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:31-35 recount Israel’s victories over Amorites and Bashan, demonstrating God’s faithfulness in giving the promised land as He vowed to the patriarchs.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the brass serpent in Numbers 21 promotes idolatry since people looked upon a metal object for healing. What does Numbers 21:8-9 actually teach about this practice?
options: The brass serpent was a divinely appointed means to look by faith for healing
The people were worshipping the brass serpent as a god
The serpent was magical and independent of God’s power
The practice was condemned immediately by Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The brass serpent was a divinely appointed means to look by faith for healing
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:8-9 records God commanding Moses to make the brass serpent as a remedy for serpent bites, teaching that healing came by God’s provision and faith, not idolatry.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining Numbers 21:2-3 and Numbers 21:24-25 about Israel’s conquest of Canaanite lands?
options: God enables Israel to fulfill their vows through divine military victory
Israel conquers lands purely by their own strength
God’s promises are conditional on Israel’s perfect obedience
The conquest was a result of political alliances
questions.correctAnswer: God enables Israel to fulfill their vows through divine military victory
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:2-3 shows Israel’s vow and God’s delivery of Canaanites, while 21:24-25 recounts victory over Sihon and possession of his cities, teaching that God empowers His people to fulfill commitments.

questions.question: What does Numbers 21:14-15 reveal about the role of Israel’s history of divine warfare in shaping their identity and faith?
options: The 'book of the wars of the LORD' records divine acts to strengthen Israel’s trust
Israel’s history is primarily human military exploits
The wars had no spiritual significance
Israel relied on foreign gods in battles
questions.correctAnswer: The 'book of the wars of the LORD' records divine acts to strengthen Israel’s trust
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:14-15 cites a record of God’s mighty acts in battle, emphasizing that Israel’s identity is rooted in divine intervention and covenant faithfulness.
